samples.summary: New destination-cell deletion path in moveRangeTo clears cells without consuming their spill-blocker registration, so a #SPILL-blocked anchor stays blocked forever
samples.evidence: The delta adds full spill cleanup when clearing destination cells covered by the propagated merge (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2394-2420), but unlike the two other paths that delete cell content it never calls `consumeSpillBlocker`. Compare `setData` (sheet.ts:1082-1086: `const blockedAnchor = this.consumeSpillBlocker(targetSref); ... dependantsMap.set(blockedAnchor, new Set())`) and `removeData` (sheet.ts:1151-1166, which collects `unblockedAnchors` and injects them into the recalculation). If the destination cell being cleared here was the registered blocker of a spill anchored outside the moved block, the entry in `this.spillBlockers` (sheet.ts:960) survives the deletion and the blocked anchor is never re-queued, so it keeps `spillBlocked: true` / ErrValue.REF (calculator.ts:115-126) even though nothing blocks it any more. The stale map entry can also later fire against an unrelated edit to that address.

samples.summary: moveRangeTo leaves orphaned spill ghosts: the main destination write (setGrid) and the source-clearing loop bypass the spill cleanup contract the delta just codified
samples.evidence: The delta adds ghost-deletion + blocker clearing for merge-covered destination cells (sheet.ts:2396-2415), duplicating the `removeData` contract. The two sibling paths in the same function do not: (1) `await this.setGrid(movedGrid)` at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2323 overwrites arbitrary destination cells, and if one of them is a spill anchor (`spillRows`/`spillCols`), its ghost cells are never deleted and keep `spillAnchor` pointing at an address that is no longer an anchor — exactly the orphan state calculator.ts:74-85 and sheet.ts:1126-1140 exist to prevent; (2) the source-clearing loop skips ghosts wholesale (`if (sourceCell?.spillAnchor) continue;`, sheet.ts:2351) while the *anchor* itself is copied to the destination with its `spillRows`/`spillCols` intact (movedGrid built at sheet.ts:2310-2315), so the ghosts stay at the source referencing a vanished anchor and are treated as read-only forever (sheet.ts:1119, 4111, 2592). Fix belongs in moveRangeTo, which now half-implements the cleanup contract.

samples.summary: Merge propagation re-creates a merge at the destination without the frozen-pane guard `canMergeSelection` enforces, so a drag-move can produce a merge straddling a frozen boundary
samples.evidence: `canMergeSelection` refuses to create any merge that crosses the frozen row/column boundary (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4292-4300), and `mergeSelection` is gated on it (sheet.ts:4319). The propagation path re-creates the merge purely by translating the anchor — `await this.store.setMerge(anchor, merge.span)` at sheet.ts:2382 — with no frozen-pane check, so dragging a merged block from inside the frozen pane to a range spanning the boundary (or vice versa) installs exactly the merge the guard forbids; the renderer/hit-test consumers (`getMerges()` at view/worksheet.ts:5557, 5638, 5708, 6002) then have to draw one rect across two panes. The delta's added invalidation makes this propagation path recalculate through the new (illegal) aliases as well.

samples.summary: Feeding merge-covered alias srefs into `calculate` lets the spill ghost logic compute ghost positions from the covered ref instead of the merge anchor
samples.evidence: The delta adds every merge-covered sref to `changedSrefs` (sheet.ts:2371, 2391), which `calculate` then iterates. Inside `calculate`, `cell` is fetched through the alias-normalising `sheet.getCell(ref)` (sheet.ts:930-931) but the ghost refs are derived from the raw covered `ref`: `const ghostRef = { r: ref.r + dr, c: ref.c + dc }` at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts:78 and the ghost write at calculator.ts:140-141. So when a merge anchor holds a spilling formula, visiting a covered alias sref writes/deletes ghosts at offsets relative to the covered cell rather than the anchor, scattering ghost cells outside the merge. The same shape is reachable via mergeSelection (sheet.ts:4328-4354), so this may predate the delta; confirming needs a test with a spilling formula inside a merged block that is drag-moved.

verdict.reason: The absence is real and I could not find any recovery path. `consumeSpillBlocker` (sheet.ts:977) has exactly two callers in the whole repo — `setData` (sheet.ts:1082-1086) and `removeData` (sheet.ts:1151-1152, 1163-1166) — and the new destination-clear loop in `moveRangeTo` (sheet.ts:2389-2421) deletes/strips cell content (2416-2420) while only calling `clearSpillBlockers` for the anchor-side cases (2401, 2414). Indirect rehabilitation is ruled out: `calculator.ts` has no blocked-anchor sweep and re-derives blocked state only for anchors it is asked to evaluate (calculator.ts:74-130); `moveRangeTo` recalculates only changed srefs and their formula-reference dependants (sheet.ts:2430-2434 with store/memory.ts:323-342), and a spill anchor does not reference its spill-target region, so the blocked anchor is never queued; `recalculateAllFormulaCells` (sheet.ts:1490) would fix stale entries but is invoked only at sheet.ts:1308, 1478, 3472, never from `moveRangeTo`, and the sole caller `view/worksheet.ts:4310` merely re-renders. Result: a spill anchored outside the moved block stays `spillBlocked: true` / ErrValue.REF (calculator.ts:118-126) with a stale entry in `this.spillBlockers`. In-lane as a violated invariant that the calculator and the two sibling deletion paths depend on; impact major.

(1) sheet.ts:2323 calls setGrid, which is a bare pass-through to store.setGrid (sheet.ts:944-946) with zero spill handling, so overwriting a destination spill anchor orphans its ghosts; the later calculate() cannot repair this because it skips non-formula srefs (calculator.ts:49-51) and only clears ghosts when the anchor still carries spillRows (calculator.ts:74-85). Orphaned ghosts are then permanently read-only to other consumers (sheet.ts:1041, 1119, 2592, 4111) and spillBlockers entries leak. The path is reachable from the drag-move handler (packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4310); moveRangeTo's only early returns concern pivots, zero delta, and partial merge coverage (sheet.ts:2265, 2281, 2294-2303) — none about spills. This is a cross-module invariant violation evidenced outside the diff, so it is in the blast-radius lane and blocking at major.

finding.summary: Merge propagation re-creates a merge at the destination without the frozen-pane guard `canMergeSelection` enforces, so a drag-move can produce a merge straddling a frozen boundary
finding.evidence: `canMergeSelection` refuses to create any merge that crosses the frozen row/column boundary (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4292-4300), and `mergeSelection` is gated on it (sheet.ts:4319). The propagation path re-creates the merge purely by translating the anchor — `await this.store.setMerge(anchor, merge.span)` at sheet.ts:2382 — with no frozen-pane check, so dragging a merged block from inside the frozen pane to a range spanning the boundary (or vice versa) installs exactly the merge the guard forbids; the renderer/hit-test consumers (`getMerges()` at view/worksheet.ts:5557, 5638, 5708, 6002) then have to draw one rect across two panes. The delta's added invalidation makes this propagation path recalculate through the new (illegal) aliases as well.

verdict.reason: The finding's factual core (no frozen check on the merge-propagation path in moveRangeTo, sheet.ts:2376-2383) is accurate, but the invariant it depends on — "no merge may straddle a frozen boundary" — is not enforced or assumed anywhere in the repo, so nothing downstream is broken. Counterexamples: Sheet.setFreezePane (sheet.ts:466-470) writes the freeze position with no merge validation whatsoever, and it is reachable from the freeze-handle drag (view/worksheet.ts:2896-2935 -> view/worksheet.ts:436-443) and from a double-click quick-freeze that sets frozenRows/Cols to 1 unconditionally (view/worksheet.ts:1341-1351). Merging A1:A3 and then double-clicking the row freeze handle already installs exactly the "illegal" straddling merge, with no involvement of moveRangeTo. Row/column moves and insert/delete likewise translate merges via moveMergeMap/shiftMergeMap without any frozen check (sheet.ts:1262, sheet.ts:1451). The named consumers also handle the state gracefully rather than relying on the invariant: the merge map is built sheet-wide (view/gridcanvas.ts:1891-1912) and every frozen quadrant is drawn inside an explicit ctx.clip() rect (view/gridcanvas.ts:280-316), so a straddling merge is simply clipped per pane — no crash, no data loss, no permission bypass; the model-side merges/mergeCoverMap are frozen-agnostic. canMergeSelection's frozen test is therefore a UI restriction on the merge action, not a contract other modules depend on, so this is at most a minor cosmetic inconsistency and not blocking under the blast-radius rubric (no broken caller, no bypassed damaging guard, no violated relied-upon invariant).

finding.summary: Feeding merge-covered alias srefs into `calculate` lets the spill ghost logic compute ghost positions from the covered ref instead of the merge anchor
finding.evidence: The delta adds every merge-covered sref to `changedSrefs` (sheet.ts:2371, 2391), which `calculate` then iterates. Inside `calculate`, `cell` is fetched through the alias-normalising `sheet.getCell(ref)` (sheet.ts:930-931) but the ghost refs are derived from the raw covered `ref`: `const ghostRef = { r: ref.r + dr, c: ref.c + dc }` at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts:78 and the ghost write at calculator.ts:140-141. So when a merge anchor holds a spilling formula, visiting a covered alias sref writes/deletes ghosts at offsets relative to the covered cell rather than the anchor, scattering ghost cells outside the merge. The same shape is reachable via mergeSelection (sheet.ts:4328-4354), so this may predate the delta; confirming needs a test with a spilling formula inside a merged block that is drag-moved.

verdict.reason: Verified in the tree, not taken on faith. `calculate` gates on `sheet.hasFormula(ref)` (calculator.ts:49), which resolves through the merge cover map (`hasFormula` -> `getCell` -> `normalizeRefToAnchor`, sheet.ts:986-989, 930-931, 796-798), so a merge-covered alias sref passes the gate and loads the ANCHOR's cell (calculator.ts:53) including its spillRows/spillCols. But every ghost coordinate is derived from the raw covered `ref`: the pre-clear loop `{ r: ref.r + dr, c: ref.c + dc }` (calculator.ts:78), the blocker probe (calculator.ts:107), and the ghost write `setCell(ghostRef, { v, spillAnchor: sref })` (calculator.ts:140-141) — while the anchor write at calculator.ts:136 IS normalised by `setCell` (sheet.ts:937-938). That asymmetry means visiting an alias re-evaluates the anchor's formula and scatters ghost cells at offsets from the covered cell, tagged with a non-anchor `spillAnchor`. Covered srefs are fed in unconditionally: `expandChangedSrefsWithMergeAliases` (sheet.ts:867-882) expands any changed sref into the whole merged block and passes it to `calculate` at the delta's move path (sheet.ts:2370-2371, 2389-2391, 2431-2433) and at many other call sites (sheet.ts:1078-1089, 1159-1168, 2486, 2666, 4133-4135, 4352-4354, 4394-4396). Example: merge A1:B1 with a 3-row spilling formula at A1 — visiting A1 writes ghosts A2/A3 (spillAnchor 'A1'), then visiting alias B1 writes ghosts at B2/B3 (spillAnchor 'B1'), outside the merge; user data at B2 would also wrongly mark the anchor #REF! via the mis-offset blocker probe. No guard blocks this: `canMergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4285-4302) checks only pivot/selection/collapsed/frozen/overlap and never spill state, and `calculate` contains no anchor-vs-alias filter. This is a blast-radius issue by construction — the broken consumer (calculator.ts) is outside the diff and its "ref is a real anchor cell" invariant is violated by the srefs the diff now supplies. Impact is incorrect/stray cell writes outside the merged block, so it is blocking at major even though the same shape may be reachable pre-delta via mergeSelection (which I am instructed not to weigh).

finding.summary: New destination-clearing loop deletes cells without the `spillAnchor` guard used elsewhere in the same method, so it can orphan spill ghost cells
finding.evidence: The pre-existing source-clearing loop skips spill cells at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2350-2352 (`if (sourceCell?.spillAnchor) continue;`). The new loop at sheet.ts:2382-2393 unconditionally `store.delete(ref)` / `store.set(ref,{s})`, bypassing that guard and the ghost cleanup `setGrid` performs for spill anchors (sheet.ts:1119-1162). A destination cell under the moved merge that is a spill ghost, or a spill anchor whose ghosts extend outside the merge, is left with dangling spill state. Fix belongs on the new code in moveRangeTo.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the new destination-clearing loop in moveRangeTo unconditionally deletes/rewrites cells without the `spillAnchor` guard. The code is not as described. The loop at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2389-2421 contains, before any mutation: a ghost guard `if (cell.spillAnchor) continue;` at sheet.ts:2397, and full spill-anchor ghost cleanup at sheet.ts:2400-2412 that calls `clearSpillBlockers` and walks the entire spillRows x spillCols rectangle (not limited to the merge bounds, so ghosts extending outside the merge are handled), deleting only cells whose `spillAnchor === sref` and recording them in `changedSrefs`; plus `else if (cell.spillBlocked) clearSpillBlockers(sref)` at 2413-2415. Only after that does it do `store.set(ref,{s})` / `store.delete(ref)` at 2416-2420. This mirrors the `removeData` cleanup contract at sheet.ts:1119-1147 that the finding cites as the correct pattern. The reviewer's quoted range 2382-2393 is truncated three lines above the guard (2382-2383 are setMerge/merges.set; 2392 is the anchor/movedGrid skip). Other nearby deletions are separate and guarded: source clear at 2350-2352, and the cut-paste source clear at 2196-2205 belongs to `paste`, guarded at 2201. No unguarded destination deletion path exists.
